tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

"""Screenshot canvas boards with the canvas's own Design Component runtime, so <dc-import> boards render whole
(render.py draws them blank). Serves <project dir> on a local port with ./support.js = the runtime saved from the
artifact's artifact-type/dc-runtime.js and /_blob/<id> mapped by blobs.json, then runs headless Chrome with its own
--user-data-dir. Usage: render_dc.py <work dir holding project/ and runtime/> <out dir> [--dark] <board.dc.html>..."""
import functools, http.server, json, re, socketserver, subprocess, sys, tempfile, threading
from pathlib import Path
args = sys.argv[1:]
dark = '--dark' in args
if dark: args.remove('--dark')
work, out, names = Path(args[0]), Path(args[1]), args[2:]
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
proj, runtime = work / 'project', work / 'runtime'
blobs = json.loads((runtime / 'blobs.json').read_text()) if (runtime / 'blobs.json').exists() else {}
chrome = '/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome'
class H(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
    def translate_path(self, path):
        p = path.split('?')[0]
        if p.endswith('/support.js'): return str(runtime / 'dc-runtime.js')
        if p.startswith('/_blob/'):
            b = blobs.get(p[7:])
            if b: return str(runtime / b)
        return super().translate_path(path)
    def do_GET(self):
        # --dark: the board's theme prop defaults to dark, the way the canvas's Theme switch sets it.
        if dark and self.path.split('?')[0].endswith('.dc.html') and 'board=1' in self.path:
            s = Path(self.translate_path(self.path)).read_text()
            s = s.replace('"theme":{"editor":"enum","options":["light","dark"],"default":"light"}', '"theme":{"editor":"enum","options":["light","dark"],"default":"dark"}')
            b = s.encode(); self.send_response(200); self.send_header('Content-Type', 'text/html; charset=utf-8'); self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(b))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(b); return
        return super().do_GET()
srv = socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), functools.partial(H, directory=str(proj)))
srv.daemon_threads = True
threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
port = srv.server_address[1]
for name in names:
    s = (proj / name).read_text()
    m = re.search(r'"\$preview":\{"width":(\d+),"height":(\d+)\}', s)
    w, h = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))
    png = out / (name.replace('.dc.html', '') + ('-dark' if dark else '') + '.png')
    subprocess.run([chrome, '--headless=new', '--disable-gpu', '--no-first-run', f'--user-data-dir={tempfile.mkdtemp()}', '--hide-scrollbars', f'--window-size={w},{h}', '--force-device-scale-factor=2',

input.description: Read the cold-reader check instructions

content.content:
9:These steps apply to every change to text a person sees, not only to new screens: a new link on an existing board, a reworded line, or a one-sentence fix all get the cold-reader check on the board before building (step 5) and in the running app after (step 8).
10-
11-1. **Start from the person.** Before drawing, write down in two or three sentences who reaches this screen, what they know at that moment, what they came to do, and what they must decide here. Every line on the screen serves one of those.
12-2. **Draw the whole screen, not a component alone.** A board for review is the full screen at the app's size, with the header, panes and neighbouring content the person really sees there, on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). Build it from the Design System artifact's coded components and the app's own markup, never by copying an older board. Repeated compositions are imported by name, as [Design handoff requirements](design-system.md#design-handoff-requirements) rule 9 says.
13-3. **Fill it with real strings.** Text that summarises data comes from the rule that will produce it in the app, run on real data. If only a model could write a line, say so on the board.
14-4. **Write every line by the wording rule below.**
15:5. **Run the cold-reader check on the boards** (below). Rewrite and check again until every line and button reads as intended.
16-6. **Show the board for review by what a person sees.** Name the screen as the person would ("the welcome screen, after typing an email"), give the canvas page it is on, and attach the picture. Board ids and builder labels mean nothing to a reviewer.
17-7. **Build it** following [Writing UI code](design-system.md#writing-ui-code).
18:8. **Check it in the running app.** Take screenshots of the built screen along one real path and run the cold-reader check again. The guards prove the code went through the tokens; only the screenshots show what the person reads.
19-
20:## The cold-reader check
21-
22-The writer of a screen cannot see that its text is cryptic, so the check is done by a reader who knows nothing about how the screen works.
23-
24-- Start a fresh agent. Give it only the screenshots and one or two sentences a real user would know (for example: "You own a 3D printer and just installed JusPrin, a desktop app that prepares 3D models for printing."). Give it no code, spec, design notes, chat history or list of suspected problems, and rename files so their names don't hint at anything.
25-- Use screenshots from one coherent path, in the order a person meets them. Mixing signed-in and signed-out screens, or states set by hand, makes the reader report contradictions that no user would see.
26-- Ask it, for each screen, to quote every line and every button exactly, say in one plain sentence what the line means or what the button will do, and list where it would hesitate, misread, worry, or not know what to do next, including information the screen leaves out. Tell it to read literally, like a busy newcomer: a line it had to puzzle out counts as a problem even if it worked it out.
27-- Compare its answers with the intent written in step 1. Any line it reads differently from the intent gets rewritten, however small the gap. Its other hesitations are input to weigh, not orders.
28-
29-What the check is known to catch: on 2026-11-06 a fresh agent given only the review's ten screenshots fully caught 14 of the 23 problems and partly caught 4 more. It caught every cryptic phrasing in the list. It missed problems that need knowledge from outside the screen (that Skip installs a 250 mm Klipper printer) and finer editorial calls (a redundant reassurance, one allowance under three names, "Connected" used for an account). It also raised real questions the review had not, such as what happens after the free month. It has not been compared with a real first-time user, so for the screens that matter most, such as first launch, a person remains the final test.
30-
31-## Wording
32-
33-Every line says what the person does or what happens to them, in a full sentence, in words a newcomer already has.
34-
35-The five patterns below are what the review found most. Each pair is the text the app showed and the review's proposed rewrite; the rewrites are proposals, not yet in the app.
36-
37-1. **Facts joined by a middle dot.** The dot drops how the facts relate, and the reader guesses.
38-   - Before: "Signed in as new@example.com · 500 credits" (reads like a balance the person already had)
39-   - After: "You got 500 free credits for signing up.", with the email address on a smaller line under it
40-2. **Metaphors.** The reader has to work out what the image stands for.
41-   - Before: "New or existing account, same door."
42-   - After: a "Sign up free" button, with "Already have an account? Sign in" under it
43-   - Before: "Pick how the agent should think." (the options are ways to pay for or connect the agent)
44-   - After: "Sign up to use the AI agent, or skip it and just slice."
45-3. **Describing the mechanism instead of the action.** Say what the person does, not how the screen works inside.
--
55:Space on a screen is tight, and short text looks finished. That is how these lines get written. Shorten only after the full sentence passes the cold-reader check, and check again after shortening.

You are reading screenshots of a desktop app as a busy newcomer would. Context a real user has: you own a 3D printer and use JusPrin, a desktop app that prepares 3D models for printing and has a built-in AI assistant you chat with. Messages to the assistant cost credits, and you can buy credits or a subscription plan from a window inside the app.

Look at these image files with your Read tool, in this order:

Person A, one path over a few weeks:
1. /private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/86b13155-fbd8-4ebe-9350-16de8efc7467/scratchpad/cold/png/screen-1.png (not signed in yet, opened the prices)
2. .../cold/png/screen-2.png (signed in, has 3 credits left)
3. .../cold/png/screen-3.png (right after paying)
4. .../cold/png/screen-4.png (a couple of weeks later)
5. .../cold/png/screen-5.png
6. .../cold/png/screen-6.png
7. .../cold/png/screen-7.png (in the app's Preferences)

Person B, a different person, one screen:
8. .../cold/png/screen-8.png (this person also pays for a subscription to Obico, a separate 3D-printer monitoring service)

(Each "..." is /private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/86b13155-fbd8-4ebe-9350-16de8efc7467/scratchpad .)

Only the window or sheet in the middle of each screenshot is the subject; the 3D-print project and chat behind it are background.

For each screen:
- Quote every line of text and every button in the foreground window exactly.
- For each, say in one plain sentence what it means to you or what the button will do.
- List every place you would hesitate, misread, worry, or not know what to do next, including information you'd want that the screen leaves out (for example about money, dates, or what happens to your credits).

Read literally. A line you had to puzzle out counts as a problem even if you worked it out. Don't suggest designs; just report how you read it. Keep the whole answer under 1,500 words. Do not open any other files.

<result>I read all eight screenshots in order and nothing else. Screens 2, 4 and 8 repeat most of screen 1, so for those I only quote what changes.

## Screen 1: Credits and plans, signed out

**Text and what it means to me**
- "Credits and plans" is the window title. "Open in browser" shows this page in my web browser. The "X" closes the window.
- "LAUNCH CELEBRATION / Double credits on everything / Every credit pack, and every month of every plan, until 31 Jan." means I get twice the credits on anything I buy until 31 Jan.
- "Buying needs a JusPrin account. New accounts get 500 free credits for their first month." means I must sign up to pay, and signing up gives me 500 credits for a month.
- "A Standard message is 1 credit and an Expert message is 5. Only messages you send cost credits." tells me what a message costs.
- "Pay monthly" and "Pay yearly" switch the prices shown. Yearly is selected.
- Credit pack card: "+ 2× launch bonus", "$10 once", "~~500~~ 1,000 credits", "These credits never expire.", and the button "Sign up to buy". One payment of $10 gives me 1,000 credits that I keep.
- Hobby card: "+ 2× launch bonus", "$100 a year", "That's 2 months free compared with paying monthly.", "~~750~~ 1,500 credits a month", "These credits reset each month. Unused ones don't carry over.", and "Sign up to buy". It's a yearly subscription with a monthly allowance I lose if I don't use it.
- Workshop card: "+ 2× launch bonus", "$200 a year", "That's 2 months free compared with paying monthly.", "~~1,000~~ 2,000 credits a month. Standard messages cost 0 credits.", the same reset sentence, and "Sign up to buy".
- "After your first month, accounts without a plan get 50 free credits a month. Your own API key stays free and never uses credits." means I get a small free amount each month, and something called an API key is another way to use the assistant.

**Where I hesitated**
- I can't see the monthly price. I'd have to work backwards from "2 months free" to get about $10 and $20 a month.
- I don't know what makes a message "Standard" or "Expert", or which one I'd need.
- Workshop says Standard messages cost 0 credits. Then are its 2,000 credits only for Expert messages? Is Standard unlimited?
- "Only messages you send cost credits" made me ask: as opposed to what? The replies? Long chats?
- If I pay yearly now, only the months up to 31 Jan are doubled. The card prints the doubled figure, so it reads as if I get it all year. I also don't know which 31 Jan is meant.
- I can't compare the options. $10 gives 1,000 credits once, and $100 gives 750 a month after the launch. Nothing helps me work out which one is cheaper for me.
- Are the 500 sign-up credits doubled too?
- If I only buy credit packs, am I one of the "accounts without a plan" who get 50 a month?
- I don't know what an "API key" is.
- There's no currency or tax shown.
- The Credit pack button is a plain outline while the other two are filled. Is it unavailable, or just less recommended?

## Screen 2: Signed in, 3 credits left

**What changed from screen 1**
- The grey line now says: "You have 3 credits and no plan. What you buy goes to alex@example.com and is ready as soon as this closes."
- Credit pack card adds a ticked box: "Auto-reload: buy another pack when I drop below 10 credits / Charged to the card used for this pack." That means automatic $10 charges.
- A second ticked box: "Tell me if a plan would have cost me less / Once, above the message box in JusPrin." That means a one-time tip in the chat.
- The buttons are now "Buy a credit pack", "Subscribe to Hobby yearly" and "Subscribe to Workshop yearly".
- The footer line about 50 free credits and the API key is gone.

**Where I hesitated**
- Auto-reload is ticked for me already. Turning on a repeating charge by default worries me. Is there a cap? Does each reload cost $10 and give 1,000 credits?
- "The card used for this pack" confused me, because I haven't entered a card. Where does payment happen? I see no checkout step.
- "Ready as soon as this closes" sounds like I have to close the window myself. Does closing it early cancel the purchase?
- "Once, above the message box" could mean once ever or once a month.
- Do these two boxes affect the plans, or only the pack?
- The note about 50 free credits a month has disappeared, and I can't tell if it still applies to me.

## Screen 3: Right after paying

**Text and what it means to me**
- "+ Doubled for the launch" is a badge.
- "You're on Hobby, paid yearly" confirms what I bought.
- "$100 for the year. This month's 1,500 credits are here: 750 a month, doubled until 31 Jan. They're on alex@example.com; you now have 1,503 credits. The next ones come on 4 Dec, and the plan renews on 4 Nov 2027." I read this as: I paid $100, I have 1,500 plus my old 3, and the next refill is on 4 Dec.
- "Back to your chat" closes this.
- "A receipt is on its way to alex@example.com. Invoices are under Billing and usage." An email is coming, and invoices are somewhere else.

**Where I hesitated**
- "Renews" doesn't say I'll be charged $100 again automatically, or whether I'll be warned first.
- "They're on alex@example.com" is a strange phrase. I had to puzzle out that it means the account.
- Where is "Billing and usage"? There's no link.
- Do my old 3 credits ever expire?
- Did auto-reload from the last screen get switched on even though I bought a plan?

## Screen 4: A couple of weeks later

**What changed**
- The grey line now says: "You're on Hobby, paid yearly: 1,122 of 1,500 credits left this month. New credits come on 4 Dec, and the plan renews on 4 Nov 2027. A switch starts today, and what you paid for the rest of your year goes toward the new plan." There's also a "Billing" link.
- Hobby's button now reads "Your plan", and it does nothing. Workshop's button reads "Switch to Workshop yearly".
- The two credit-pack boxes are still ticked.

**Where I hesitated**
- "A switch starts today…" took me two reads. A switch to what?
- How much would I actually pay to move to Workshop today? The screen doesn't show a number.
- Would I keep my 1,122 credits if I switch?
- What happens if I click "Pay monthly" while I'm on a yearly plan?
- Earlier I had 1,503. The 3 extra credits have dropped out of "1,122 of 1,500", and I don't know where they went.
- Both pack boxes are ticked again. Is auto-reload already on for me?

## Screen 5: Billing and usage

**Text and what it means to me**
- "Billing and usage" is the window title and the page heading.
- Under "Plan": "Hobby · $100 a year / 1,500 credits a month until 31 Jan, then 750. New credits on 4 Dec. Renews 4 Nov 2027." The buttons are "Change plan" and "Cancel plan". This is my plan and when it refills.
- "Payment method and invoices / Visa ending 4242. Receipts for every payment and credit pack." The "Open" button shows my card and receipts.
- Under "Credits and usage": "1,122 credits left / Expiring credits are used first." with a "Buy a credit pack" link.
- "Auto-reload is on / Buys a credit pack ($10, 1,000 credits during the launch) whenever you drop below 10 credits." The buttons are "Change" and "Turn off".
- "438 credits / used in the last 30 days", then a bar chart labelled "55", "21 Oct", "5 Nov" and "19 Nov".
- A table with columns "Date / Chat / Tier / Messages / Credits". The rows are "19 Nov / Resizing a Print to Fit the Bambu A1 mini / Expert / 8 / 40" and "18 Nov / Stringing on a PETG Bracket / Stan… / 18 / 18".

**Where I hesitated**
- Auto-reload is on, and I only bought a plan. That alarms me. Will it charge me $10 at the end of a month just before my monthly credits refill?
- "Expiring credits are used first" left me unsure which of my credits expire.
- The numbers don't add up for me. I used 438 credits, but only 378 are gone from my 1,500.
- The chart starts on 21 Oct, before I subscribed.
- "55" has no unit.
- "Stan…" is cut off.
- "Open" doesn't say where it goes.

## Screen 6: Cancel confirmation

**Text and what it means to me**
- "Cancel Hobby?"
- "You keep Hobby until 4 Nov 2027, with new credits each month until then, and it doesn't renew. Nothing is refunded. Credit packs you bought stay." Clear: I keep it until it runs out, and get no money back.
- "Keep Hobby" changes nothing. "Cancel plan" stops the renewal.

**Where I hesitated**
- What do I get after 4 Nov 2027? Back to 50 free credits a month?
- Does auto-reload keep charging my card after I cancel?
- "Credit packs you bought" confused me, because I never bought one myself. Does it mean packs that auto-reload bought?
- Can I undo a cancellation?

## Screen 7: Preferences, deleting the account

**Text and what it means to me**
- The sidebar lists "Account", "BYOAI / Bring Your Own AI", "Appearance", "3D view", "Projects & files" and "Updates".
- Below that: "More preferences… / The full preferences window from OrcaSlicer, which JusPrin is built on." That opens older, fuller settings.
- The Account section shows "JusPrin account / Signed in as alex@example.com" with a "Sign out" button.
- It shows "Hobby / $100 a year. Renews 4 Nov 2027." with "Billing and usage" and "Get more credits" buttons. Partly hidden behind the dialog: "1,122 of 1,500 left".
- Also behind the dialog: "Ends any plan and removes this account's credits and everything JusPrin keeps for it on its servers." with a "Delete account…" button.
- The dialog reads "Delete your JusPrin account?" and then: "Your Hobby plan ends today, and the 1,122 credits left on alex@example.com are removed with everything JusPrin keeps for this account. The months left of your year aren't refunded. This can't be undone." The buttons are "Cancel" and "Delete account".

**Where I hesitated**
- "Everything JusPrin keeps" doesn't tell me what that is. My chats? My projects? Files on my computer?
- Does deleting remove my saved card and stop auto-reload? It's implied, not stated.
- "Cancel" here closes the dialog, but on the last screen "Cancel plan" meant ending the plan. In a delete dialog that made me pause.
- "BYOAI" means nothing to me until I read the second line.
- Can I sign up again later with the same email and get the 500 free credits again?

## Screen 8: Person B, an Obico Premium subscriber

**What changed**
- The grey line now says: "You have 3 credits and no plan. As an Obico Premium subscriber on alex@example.com, you get 20% off Hobby and Workshop for as long as you keep the plan."
- Hobby shows "~~$100~~ $80 a year / With Obico Premium's 20% off. That's 2 months free compared with paying monthly."
- Workshop shows "~~$200~~ $160 a year" with the same sentence.
- The Credit pack card and all the buttons are the same as on screen 2.

**Where I hesitated**
- "As long as you keep the plan" could mean my Obico plan or this JusPrin plan. I can't tell which.
- If I stop paying for Obico, does the price jump when this plan renews?
- "2 months free compared with paying monthly" sits next to 20% off. Is the monthly price also 20% off? Is it 2 months free on top of the 20%?
- Credit packs get no discount, and nothing says so.
- I don't know how it matched my Obico subscription. By the same email?</result>

# Yearly Hobby and Workshop plans for everyone: proposal

Status, 2026-11-10:
- **Kenneth decided:** JusPrin 1's 15 yearly subscribers move to a yearly Hobby plan, and the yearly plans are offered to everyone.
- **Proposed:** everything else below. Nothing is built, and no Chargebee site has changed.
- **Kenneth decided:** the yearly prices are $100 for Hobby and $200 for Workshop.
- **Open:** whether the Obico 20% applies to yearly plans. Shown here at my pick (yes).

## What a yearly plan is

- It is the same Hobby or Workshop plan, paid once a year.
- Credits still come every month (750 or 1,000), and unused ones don't carry over, as on the monthly plans.
- The launch bonus doubles each month's credits until 31 Jan, as it does on the monthly plans.

## JusPrin 1's yearly subscribers (runbook, by hand)

1. On `jusprinv2`, create the customer `jusprinv2-<user id>`.
2. Create a yearly Hobby subscription with its price overridden to $59.99 (one person: $41.99), plus the coupon `jusprin1-move-first-term` (100% off, once).
3. Change its term end to their JusPrin 1 renewal date, without proration. They pay nothing until that date, then $59.99 a year on the same date as before.
4. Cancel JusPrin 1 on Obico's site now, with no refund.

Steps 2 and 3 need one check on `jusprinv2-test` first.

## What each page shows

**Credits and plans** (server page)
- A choice above the cards: "Pay monthly" and "Pay yearly". It's two links, and the server draws the chosen one. Monthly is the default, and someone already on a yearly plan sees yearly first.
- The Credit pack card is the same in both.
- Hobby, yearly:
  - "$100 a year"
  - "That's 2 months free compared with paying monthly."
  - "750 credits a month."
  - "These credits reset each month. Unused ones don't carry over."
  - Button: "Subscribe to Hobby yearly"
- Workshop, yearly: "$200 a year", "1,000 credits a month. Standard messages cost 0 credits.", and the button "Subscribe to Workshop yearly".
- An Obico Premium subscriber sees "$100" struck through, then "$80 a year", "With Obico Premium's 20% off."
- Top line for someone on yearly Hobby: "You're on Hobby, paid yearly: 512 of 750 credits left this month. You get 750 new credits on 4 Dec, and the plan renews on 4 Aug 2027."
- Switch lines:
  - From yearly to monthly: "A switch starts today. What's left of your year comes off the new plan's payments."
  - From monthly to yearly: "A switch starts today. You pay for the year now, less what's left of this month."
- Buttons: "Switch to Hobby yearly", "Switch to Workshop monthly", and so on. The plan they're on reads "Your plan".

**Checkout finished** (server page)
- "You're on Hobby, paid yearly"
- "750 credits a month, doubled until 31 Jan. They're on alex@example.com; you now have 1,500 credits."

**Billing and usage** (server page)
- "Hobby", "$100 a year", "750 credits a month. Renews 4 Aug 2027."
- A JusPrin 1 mover sees "$59.99 a year".
- Change plan, Cancel plan, the payment method and invoices stay as they are.

**Cancel plan** (server page)
- "Cancel Hobby?"
- "You keep Hobby until 4 Aug 2027, with 750 credits each month until then, and it doesn't renew. Nothing is refunded. Credit packs you bought stay."
- A JusPrin 1 mover also sees: "The $59.99 price isn't offered again after it ends."

**Preferences > Account** (app)
- "Hobby" and "$100 a year. Renews 4 Aug 2027."
- The price sentence is the server's. The app adds the year to a date that isn't in the current year, which is a small app change.

**Credit bars in the message box and on Home's AI card** (app)
- Unchanged: "Hobby credits", "512 of 750 left", "Expires 4 Dec. Unused credits don't carry over."

**Delete account confirmation** (the server's words, shown by the app)
- Adds, for a yearly plan: "The months of your year that are left aren't refunded."
- This is if Chargebee refunds nothing on an immediate cancel, which I'll check.

**Chargebee's emails on the JusPrin site:** the renewal reminder before a yearly renewal joins the emails that still need JusPrin wording.

## Server and app work

- **Chargebee, both JusPrin sites:**
  - The item prices `jusprin-hobby-yearly` ($100) and `jusprin-workshop-yearly` ($200).
  - The coupon `jusprin2-obico-premium-20` extended to both of those prices.
  - The coupon `jusprin1-move-first-term`, for the movers.
- **settings_ent:**
  - Each plan gets a period and the monthly plan it pairs with.
  - Hobby and Workshop are listed once each, with a monthly and a yearly price.
- **Credits:**
  - A yearly term grants its monthly credits once a month, each lot lasting a month, created lazily the way the free credits are.
  - Switching between plans ends the earlier plan's lots, as today, and a lot still waits for its payment.
- **Prices and wording:**
  - The billed price and period are stored from Chargebee on the plan record.
  - This also fixes the app showing $10 to a mover at $6.99, or $8 to someone whose Obico subscription ended.
- **Pages:**
  - The monthly/yearly choice and the yearly cards on Credits and plans.
  - The switch lines, the checkout-finished line, and the billing and cancel wording.
  - Years on dates that aren't in the current year.
- **Tests** for each of the above.

The estimate is 3 to 4 days of server work and an hour in the app, plus the screen boards and cold-reader checks first.

## Order

1. Kenneth decides whether the Obico 20% applies to yearly plans. (Prices: decided.)
2. Boards on the canvas's "Plan and billing" page: Credits and plans, monthly and yearly, signed out, signed in, and as an Obico subscriber; then checkout finished, Billing and usage, Cancel plan, and Preferences > Account. Then a cold-reader check.

content.text:
I've added eight screens showing how the yearly plans would look, priced at $100 a year for Hobby and $200 for Workshop. They're on the Credits & plans page of the [JusPrin design canvas](https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ), in a new row titled "Yearly plans · proposal, 2026-11-10". This is only a proposal: no code is written and no Chargebee site has changed.

**The eight screens:**
- **Credits and plans, in three versions:** before signing in, signed in without a plan, and for an Obico Premium subscriber. A "Pay monthly / Pay yearly" switch sits at the right end of the line about message costs. The yearly cards read "Subscribe to Hobby yearly" and "Subscribe to Workshop yearly".
- **Credits and plans for someone already on yearly Hobby:** the line at the top gives this month's credits, the date new credits come, and the renewal date. It also says what happens to the money already paid if they switch plans.
- **Right after paying:** "You're on Hobby, paid yearly". It says the card will be charged $100 again on 4 Nov 2027 unless they cancel before then.
- **Billing and usage:** only the plan row changes, to "Hobby · $100 a year" with both dates.
- **Cancel plan:** they keep Hobby and its monthly credits until the year ends. Nothing is refunded, and afterwards they drop to 50 free credits a month.
- **Preferences › Account:** "$100 a year. Renews 4 Nov 2027." The delete-account warning adds "The months left of your year aren't refunded."

**What the wording check changed.** A fresh reviewer read the screens twice, seeing only the images and knowing nothing about the design. On the first pass it misread five of my lines, so I rewrote them:
- **The yearly price:** "2 months free" alone made it work out the monthly price. The card now says "Paying monthly costs $120 a year, so 2 months are free."
- **The monthly credits:** "1,500 credits a month" read as if the launch doubling lasted all year. It now says "1,500 credits a month until 31 Jan, then 750."
- **After paying:** "renews" didn't say the card is charged again, so that screen now says it outright.
- **Cancel:** it didn't say what comes after the paid year ends. It now does.
- **The Obico discount:** "as long as you keep the plan" could mean the Obico plan. It now says the discount stays with the JusPrin plan they buy, even if Obico ends.

On the second pass it read every main line as intended, and I fixed four small gaps it still found.

**What's still open:**
- **The Obico 20% on yearly plans** is undecided. The Obico screen shows my pick, $80 and $160 a year, and is marked "NOT DECIDED".
- **Switching plans and deleting an account:** the sentence about what a switch does with money already paid is a placeholder until I check Chargebee's proration setting on the test site. The delete warning also waits on checking that Chargebee refunds nothing when it cancels a plan at once.
- **Problems in screens that were already there:** the reviewer was alarmed to find "Auto-reload" ticked by default on the Credit pack card, and puzzled by "They're on alex@example.com". I left both alone because they aren't part of the yearly change.

The shared proposal note, `jusprin2-yearly-hobby-proposal.md`, now points to these screens.

Chargebee's documentation supports the core of your question: a downgrade can leave a refundable balance that gets applied to later invoices, though the docs differ on whether that application is automatic.

- **Downgrades create refundable credits:** Chargebee's own support article says that if a subscription change leaves a balance owed to the customer, it is applied back to the account as a refundable credit.
- **Automatic application:** The API reference says refundable credits are applied automatically when a new invoice is generated for the customer. Another API page describes retaining them for automatic application on future invoices as one of the options.
- **Refund alternative:** The same support article notes the amount can either be refunded or allocated for the upcoming invoices. So the balance is not always applied automatically. A merchant or customer can choose a refund instead.
- **Timing caveat:** Adjustment credits are different. For a downgrade made before an unpaid invoice is collected, the adjustment is directly applied to a specific, unpaid invoice, reducing its outstanding balance.

Overall, the sources agree that a refundable credit from a downgrade can carry forward to future invoices. Whether that happens automatically or as a manual choice between carry-forward and refund is less clear across the pages. I'd check the Chargebee docs for your specific site configuration before relying on automatic application.

The Chargebee test site (`jusprinv2-test`) confirms the yearly plans work as the approved screens describe. I ran four checks through Chargebee's API. They used three throwaway test customers with Stripe's test card and no email address, and their subscriptions are now cancelled.

**What I added to the test site, and kept for the build:**
- **Yearly prices:** `jusprin-hobby-yearly` at $100 a year and `jusprin-workshop-yearly` at $200 a year.
- **Free first term:** a coupon `jusprin1-move-first-term`, 100% off once, for yearly Hobby only.
- **Obico discount:** the coupon `jusprin2-obico-premium-20` now also covers both yearly prices.

The live Chargebee site needs the same three changes when it's set up. Nothing on the live site changed.

**What the checks showed:**
- **Moving a yearly JusPrin 1 subscriber:** I created yearly Hobby at their old $59.99 with the free-first-term coupon. They paid $0 now, and the subscription is active in the state the server needs to grant credits. I then moved the end of the first year to a sample JusPrin 1 renewal date, 15 Mar 2027. Chargebee made no extra charge or credit, and the next renewal is $59.99 on 15 Mar 2027 for a full year. The coupon doesn't apply again.
- **Switching from yearly Hobby to yearly Workshop:** the unused part of the Hobby year comes off the Workshop price. Right after paying, that meant $100 due, and a new year starts that day.
- **Switching from yearly Hobby to monthly Hobby:** I applied this one rather than just previewing it. Chargebee turned the unused year into $100 of credit, used $10 for the first month, and kept $90. The next month's $10 renewal came out of that credit, with $0 due. So the line "what you paid for the months left counts toward its price" holds both ways. The leftover is also marked as refundable, so it could be refunded by hand.
- **Ending a paid yearly plan at once:** I used the same call deleting an account makes today. Chargebee refunded nothing and left no credit, so the warning "The months left of your year aren't refunded" is accurate.

I wrote the results into the shared note `jusprin2-yearly-hobby-proposal.md` under "Test-site results". On the [design canvas](https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ), the two screens that said their wording waited on these checks now say the checks passed. I also told the session checking the Chargebee setup on staging what I added to the test site.

The next step is the code: about 3 to 4 days on the server and about an hour in the app.

Sources: [Chargebee: credit notes API](https://apidocs.chargebee.com/docs/api/credit_notes), [Chargebee: actions on a refundable credit note](https://support.chargebee.com/support/solutions/articles/254839-what-are-the-actions-that-can-be-performed-on-a-refundable-credit-note-)

# Yumi's mobile app sends its brand's name in X-Obico-Syndicate, but Yumi's
# accounts were on a server of their own.
SYNDICATES['kingroon'] = {'brand': 'kingroon'}
SYNDICATES['jusprinv2'] = {'brand': 'jusprinv2'}

# JusPrin v2 model gateway (web_ent/jusprin/v2). The JSON shape is documented in
# web_ent/jusprin/v2/aliases.py. The two limits are placeholders until pricing
# is decided.
JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES = os.environ.get('JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES', '')
JUSPRIN_V2_MAX_BODY_BYTES = 20 * 1024 * 1024
JUSPRIN_V2_TURNS_PER_MINUTE = 60
# The oldest JusPrin release the server serves, as "2.0.0"; older releases are
# told to update (web_ent/jusprin/v2/app_version.py). Empty serves every release.
JUSPRIN_V2_MIN_APP_VERSION = os.environ.get('JUSPRIN_V2_MIN_APP_VERSION', '')
# Credits.
JUSPRIN_V2_REPORT_CREDITS = 25
JUSPRIN_V2_REPORT_MIN_TEXT = 200
JUSPRIN_V2_REPORT_MAX_PHOTOS = 6
JUSPRIN_V2_REPORT_MAX_PHOTO_BYTES = 20 * 1024 * 1024
JUSPRIN_V2_SIGNUP_CREDITS = 500
# The OAuth2 application the desktop app signs in as; email sign-in mints its tokens.
JUSPRIN_V2_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID = 'JusPrin2'
JUSPRIN_V2_FREE_CREDITS = 50
JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS = {
    'jusprin-hobby-monthly': {'name': 'Hobby', 'cents': 1000, 'credits': 750},
    'jusprin-workshop-monthly': {'name': 'Workshop', 'cents': 2000, 'credits': 1000, 'unlimited_basic': True},
}
JUSPRIN_V1_PLANS = {
    'jusprin-unlimited-monthly': {'cents': 699, 'period': 'month'},
    'jusprin-unlimited-annual': {'cents': 5999, 'period': 'year'},
}
JUSPRIN_V2_CREDIT_CENTS = 2
# Obico Premium subscribers' discount on a JusPrin 2 plan, as the plan's price
# line in GET /v2/account states it.
JUSPRIN_V2_OBICO_DISCOUNT_PERCENT = 20
# JusPrin 2 sells on a Chargebee site of its own, apart from Obico's
# (CHARGEBEE_SITE): web_ent/jusprin/ledger/billing.py.
JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_SITE = os.environ.get('JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_SITE')
JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_API_KEY = os.environ.get('JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_API_KEY')
# A JusPrin 2 account's Chargebee customer is <prefix><user id>. Servers that
# share one Chargebee site (staging and local servers share its test site) each
# need their own prefix, or one server's events reach another's accounts.
JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_CUSTOMER_PREFIX = os.environ.get('JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_CUSTOMER_PREFIX', 'jusprinv2-')
# The credit pack: a one-off Chargebee charge, bought on a one-time checkout.
JUSPRIN_V2_PACK = {'credits': 500, 'cents': 1000}
JUSPRIN_V2_PACK_PRICE_ID = 'jusprin-credit-pack-USD'
# The Chargebee coupon a JusPrin 2 plan's checkout carries for an Obico Premium
# subscriber: JUSPRIN_V2_OBICO_DISCOUNT_PERCENT off, every month of the plan.
JUSPRIN_V2_OBICO_COUPON = 'jusprin2-obico-premium-20'
# The launch offer in the box on the app's Account page (GET /v2/account_box)
# shows until this moment, the end of 31 Jan in California; after it the box is
# empty without a deploy.
JUSPRIN_V2_LAUNCH_OFFER_ENDS = datetime.fromisoformat(
    os.environ.get('JUSPRIN_V2_LAUNCH_OFFER_ENDS', '2027-02-01T00:00:00-08:00'))
# The server's pages the app opens in its sheet, by the page name the app asks
# for in POST /v2/web_link. A link from it works once, for this many seconds.
JUSPRIN_V2_WEB_PAGES = {
    'prices': '/ent/jusprin/v2/web/prices',
    'billing': '/ent/jusprin/v2/web/billing',
}
JUSPRIN_V2_WEB_LINK_SECONDS = 60
# Bodies above this size count as large, and each process holds at most this
# many large requests at once (about 95 MiB each at the 20 MiB cap); another
# waits this long for a slot, then is told the gateway is busy.
JUSPRIN_V2_LARGE_BODY_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024
"""What JusPrin 2 sells through Chargebee, and the credits each sale grants.

JusPrin 2 sells on a Chargebee site of its own (JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_SITE),
apart from Obico's (CHARGEBEE_SITE), so its checkout, emails and invoices are
JusPrin's. Every call here passes that site; the module never uses the site
chargebee.configure() set for Obico. The site is on Chargebee's Product Catalog
2.0, so a plan or the pack is an item price and is bought with the *_for_items
calls.

The credit pack is a one-off charge (JUSPRIN_V2_PACK_PRICE_ID) bought on a
one-time checkout; its lot never expires. Hobby and Workshop are Chargebee
plans whose item price ids are JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS' keys; each term grants a lot
that expires with the term. Until JUSPRIN_V2_LAUNCH_OFFER_ENDS every lot comes with a
launch-bonus lot of the same size and expiry.

A lot is keyed by the invoice or the term that paid for it, so the checkout's
return and Chargebee's webhook can both report one sale and it counts once.

A JusPrin 2 account is a Chargebee customer of its own, jusprinv2-<user id>
(JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_CUSTOMER_PREFIX names the prefix),
apart from any Obico account with the same email (lib/syndicate.py),
so the webhook finds the account by that id and never by email.
"""
from datetime import datetime, timezone as dt_timezone
from typing import Dict, Optional

import chargebee
from chargebee.environment import Environment
from django.conf import settings
from django.db import transaction
from django.utils import timezone

from app.models import User
from jusprin.models import JusPrinPlan
from .models import CreditGrant

# Obico's own syndicate, the one an Obico Premium subscription is in.
OBICO_SYNDICATE = 'base'
SUBSCRIPTION_EVENTS = {
    'subscription_created', 'subscription_started', 'subscription_activated', 'subscription_changed',
    'subscription_cancellation_scheduled', 'subscription_cancelled', 'subscription_reactivated',
    'subscription_renewed', 'subscription_scheduled_cancellation_removed',
}
INVOICE_EVENTS = {'invoice_generated', 'payment_succeeded'}
# A plan in these states pays for its current term.
LIVE_STATUSES = {'active', 'non_renewing', 'in_trial'}


def _site() -> Environment:
    return Environment({'api_key': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_API_KEY, 'site': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_SITE})


def customer_id(user) -> str:
    return f'{settings.JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_CUSTOMER_PREFIX}{user.id}'


def user_for_customer(cb_customer_id: str) -> Optional[User]:
    prefix = settings.JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_CUSTOMER_PREFIX
    if not cb_customer_id or not cb_customer_id.startswith(prefix):
        return None
    user_id = cb_customer_id[len(prefix):]
    return User.objects.filter(id=int(user_id)).first() if user_id.isdigit() else None


def is_v2_plan(plan_id: str) -> bool:
    return plan_id in settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS


def plan_price_id(sub: Dict) -> str:
    """The subscription's plan, as its item price id, from Chargebee's
    subscription as a dict; '' when it has no plan."""
    return next((item['item_price_id'] for item in sub.get('subscription_items') or []
                 if item.get('item_type') == 'plan'), '')


def launch_on(now: datetime = None) -> bool:
    return (now or timezone.now()) < settings.JUSPRIN_V2_LAUNCH_OFFER_ENDS


def obico_premium(user) -> bool:
    """Whether the same person pays for Obico Premium: an account in Obico's own
    syndicate under this account's email with an active subscription that
    Chargebee bills (a non-empty external_id). That leaves out the free trial
    every new account starts (start_free_trial) and the free pro-comp plans,
    as JusPrin 1 does. A JusPrin 2 account's own email is always verified: it
    signs in by an emailed code or by Google."""
    from app.accounts import users_by_email
    from app.models import Syndicate
    from app_ent.models import Subscription
    obico = Syndicate.objects.filter(name=OBICO_SYNDICATE).first()
    if not user.email or obico is None:
        return False
    owners = [owner.id for owner in users_by_email(user.email, obico)]
    return any(sub.active() for sub in Subscription.objects.filter(user_id__in=owners).exclude(external_id=''))


def ensure_customer(user) -> str:
    """The account's Chargebee customer id, creating the customer the first
    time the account buys anything."""
    cb_id = customer_id(user)
    try:
        chargebee.Customer.retrieve(cb_id, env=_site())
    except chargebee.InvalidRequestError as e:
        if getattr(e, 'api_error_code', None) != 'resource_not_found':
            raise
        chargebee.Customer.create({'id': cb_id, 'email': user.email,
                                   'first_name': user.first_name, 'last_name': user.last_name}, env=_site())
    return cb_id


def pack_checkout(user, redirect_url: str) -> str:
    """The address of Chargebee's checkout for one credit pack."""
    result = chargebee.HostedPage.checkout_one_time_for_items({
        'customer': {'id': ensure_customer(user)},
        'item_prices': [{'item_price_id': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PACK_PRICE_ID, 'quantity': 1}],
        'redirect_url': redirect_url,
    }, env=_site())
    return result.hosted_page.url


def plan_checkout(user, plan_id: str, redirect_url: str) -> str:
    """The address of Chargebee's checkout for a plan: a new subscription, or a
    switch of the one the account has. An Obico Premium subscriber's carries
    the discount coupon. A coupon code, such as the one a JusPrin 1
    subscriber is emailed, goes in the checkout's own "Apply coupon" field."""
    current = JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(user=user).first()
    live = current is not None and current.external_id and current.is_active and is_v2_plan(current.plan_id)
    payload = {'redirect_url': redirect_url}
    if obico_premium(user):
        payload['coupon_ids'] = [settings.JUSPRIN_V2_OBICO_COUPON]
    # A subscription has one plan, so the new plan replaces the current one.
    payload['subscription_items'] = [{'item_price_id': plan_id}]
    if live:
        payload['subscription'] = {'id': current.external_id}
        result = chargebee.HostedPage.checkout_existing_for_items(payload, env=_site())
    else:
        payload['customer'] = {'id': ensure_customer(user)}
        result = chargebee.HostedPage.checkout_new_for_items(payload, env=_site())
    return result.hosted_page.url


def portal_url(user, redirect_url: str) -> str:
    """Chargebee's portal for the account's payment method and invoices."""
    result = chargebee.PortalSession.create({'customer': {'id': customer_id(user)}, 'redirect_url': redirect_url},
                                            env=_site())
    return result.portal_session.access_url


def card_line(user) -> Optional[str]:
    """"Visa ending 4242", or None when Chargebee has no card for the account."""
    try:
        card = chargebee.Customer.retrieve(customer_id(user), env=_site()).card
    except chargebee.APIError:
        return None
    if card is None:
        return None
    return f"{(card.card_type or 'Card').replace('_', ' ').title()} ending {card.last4}"


def end_plan_now(plan: JusPrinPlan) -> None:
    """Ends the plan now rather than at the end of its term, for a deleted
    account. A subscription Chargebee no longer has has nothing left to end."""
    try:
        status = chargebee.Subscription.retrieve(plan.external_id, env=_site()).subscription.status
    except chargebee.InvalidRequestError as e:
        if getattr(e, 'api_error_code', None) != 'resource_not_found':
            raise
        return
    if status != 'cancelled':
        chargebee.Subscription.cancel_for_items(plan.external_id, {'end_of_term': False}, env=_site())


def cancel_plan(user) -> None:
    """Stops the plan at the end of the term already paid for."""
    plan = JusPrinPlan.objects.get(user=user)
    result = chargebee.Subscription.cancel_for_items(plan.external_id, {'end_of_term': True}, env=_site())
    record_subscription(user, result.subscription.values)


def _when(seconds) -> Optional[datetime]:
